stories.summary: McMaster immunologist Manali Mukherjee has been awarded the Falling Walls Women's Impact Award in Berlin. Her research reveals the biological basis of Long COVID.
stories.title: Immunologist Manali Mukherjee receives Falling Walls Women’s Impact Award

stories.summary: A man in southern Brazil spent 12 days searching for the owner of a lost wad of cash he found in a public plaza. The money turned out to be the entire monthly salary of a young construction worker.
stories.title: Man Spends 12 Days Returning Lost Cash a Laborer Needed for His Daughter

stories.summary: Researchers studying rare whales discovered a previously unknown calf off the coast of Canada. The finding brought great joy to scientists monitoring the endangered species.
stories.title: Scientists discovered an unknown baby right whale off Canada. They say it’s a cause for joy

stories.summary: The Bangka slow loris, a primate previously believed to potentially be extinct, was found still surviving on the island of Bangka. A local wildlife organization has been actively rescuing the animals and returning them to the wild.
stories.title: Venomous Primate Believed Extinct for 100 Years Was Hiding in Plain Sight All Along

stories.summary: Vermont Gas launched the state's first community-scale geothermal project to help lower energy costs for customers. The system powers affordable housing and offers homeowners up to 40% in energy savings.
stories.title: Geothermal Utilities Power Wave of US Affordable Housing with 40% Energy Savings

stories.summary: Canada's National Advisory Committee on Immunization issued updated guidance recommending hepatitis B vaccination for all infants. The recommendation aims to prevent early childhood exposure to a virus that frequently leads to chronic liver disease.
stories.title: All infants should be vaccinated against hep B, says Canadian vaccine advisory committee

stories.summary: Artist Carsten Höller has created a permanent slide installation in Mexico City. The silver slides range from 12 to 38 meters in height.
stories.title: Carsten Höller’s Spiraling Silver Slides Appear in Mexico City as a Permanent Installation

stories.summary: Mediterranean beach resorts are adjusting operations to safely accommodate nesting loggerhead sea turtles. Local community volunteers regularly organize efforts to protect turtle nests and share shoreline space.
stories.title: As loggerhead turtles spread west, Mediterranean beach resorts learn to share the sand

stories.summary: Health Canada approved Moderna's mRNA influenza vaccine as well as a combined mRNA vaccine targeting both flu and COVID-19. The newly authorized vaccines offer expanded immunization options for Canadians ahead of respiratory virus season.
stories.title: Moderna's mRNA flu and flu-COVID combo vaccines have been approved by Health Canada

stories.summary: Imaging and chemical analysis of a 115-million-year-old dinosaur fossil indicate the presence of fossilized blood cells. While some researchers remain unconvinced, the findings offer compelling evidence of ancient cellular preservation.
stories.title: This may be the best evidence yet that dinosaur blood can fossilize

stories.summary: A health study links higher levels of beneficial body fat to a reduced frequency of anxiety and depression diagnoses. The findings indicate that different types of body fat have distinct effects on mental wellness.
stories.title: 'Good' Body Fat Is Linked to Fewer Anxiety And Depression Diagnoses

stories.summary: McMaster University is hosting Global Entrepreneurship Week from November 16 to 20 to support innovators of all backgrounds. The event features workshops, panel discussions, and competitions for budding entrepreneurs.
stories.title: Entrepreneurs Thrive Here: Celebrating Global Entrepreneurship Week at McMaster

stories.summary: McMaster University held its fifth annual Indigenous Research Day to highlight impactful community-based research. The event brought together faculty, researchers, and community members at CIBC Hall.
stories.title: Research that reflects communities: Indigenous Research Day 2026

stories.summary: Residents in Juneau, Alaska maintain long-standing traditions of sharing food within their community to overcome harsh local growing conditions. Despite geographical isolation and limited farmland, neighbors support one another through mutual sharing.
stories.title: In Alaska’s capital, food comes by water, air or, most often, community sharing

stories.summary: McMaster University introduced a new concurrent certificate combining history studies with education training. The program prepares students for careers in teaching, public history, and museum work.
stories.title: McMaster launches new certificate linking history studies with careers in education

stories.summary: Fossil evidence reveals that the ancient armored amphibian Gerrothorax maritimus lived and hunted on the seafloor about 237 million years ago. It is the first known amphibian to exist entirely without access to land or freshwater.
stories.title: This armored amphibian once lived and hunted on the seafloor

stories.summary: Researchers demonstrated that a novel drug treatment restored liver function and lowered cholesterol in aging rats. The therapy also halved the levels of a key protein associated with Alzheimer's disease.
stories.title: Drug Restores Liver Function in Aging Rats And Halves Levels of an Alzheimer's-Linked Protein

stories.summary: Waterloo region is hosting several community events over the weekend including film festivals and Diwali celebrations. Residents can also participate in holiday markets and a tree of the year event.
stories.title: Kate's 5 fun things to do in and around Waterloo region this weekend: Nov. 6 to 8

stories.summary: A group of Canadian youth is running initiatives to help the public understand how climate change impacts brain health. Environmental programs are also featuring community strategies to keep post-Halloween pumpkins out of landfills.
stories.title: Canadian youth are helping others understand how climate change affects the brain

stories.summary: Scientists discovered preserved biological traces of ancient blood inside 115-million-year-old dinosaur bones. The finding challenges long-held assumptions about molecular survival and offers new insights into ancient physiology.
stories.title: Scientists just found dinosaur blood that survived 115 million years

stories.summary: Kenya launched a 10-year conservation program covering 17.3 million hectares of protected and community lands. The initiative aims to expand conserved areas while benefiting 1.6 million local residents.
stories.title: Kenya launches $160 million conservation initiative to support communities and biodiversity

stories.summary: Recent global progress includes large-scale ecosystem restoration projects across multiple regions. Additionally, Barbados successfully eliminated mother-to-child HIV transmission.
stories.title: What went right this week: the good news that matters

stories.summary: Researchers are studying the remarkable ability of octopuses to navigate extremely tight openings. The biological mechanisms allowing their flexible bodies to pass through tiny gaps continue to fascinate scientists.
stories.title: Octopuses Can Squeeze Their Bodies Through Tiny Holes, And Scientists Are in Awe

stories.summary: A clinical trial involving nearly 5,800 adults demonstrated that heart scans can effectively guide statin prescriptions while reducing unnecessary medication. Patients prescribed statins based on scan results were significantly more likely to adhere to their treatment.
stories.title: Major trial challenges how doctors decide who really needs statins

stories.summary: A juvenile orangutan rescued from illegal possession in Mumbai was successfully repatriated to Indonesia. Conservation experts are now preparing the endangered animal for its eventual return to the wild.
stories.title: India repatriates seized orangutan, raising hopes for five more

stories.summary: November's night sky features bright meteor fireballs, a close planetary pairing, and a prominent supermoon. Meanwhile, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft achieved a milestone by reaching one light-day distance from Earth.
stories.title: Don't miss: Meteor showers, fireballs, and a supermoon light up November's night sky

stories.summary: Community land ownership models are successfully maintaining long-term affordable housing options. Local groups are taking collective action to create lasting positive change in their neighborhoods.
stories.title: The Spark: When Communities Own the Land, Housing Stays Affordable

stories.summary: King Henry III signed the Charter of the Forest 809 years ago in England to grant common people access to Royal forests. The historic document expanded rights beyond the Magna Carta by allowing free men to use forest resources.
stories.title: Good News in History, November 6

stories.summary: Researchers confirmed the presence of horseshoe crabs in the Philippine province of Tawi-Tawi for the first time. The discovery expands the known range of the species and supports local conservation efforts.
stories.title: Scientists confirm horseshoe crabs in a second Philippine province, urge conservation

stories.summary: NASA's Swift Observatory has re-entered Earth's atmosphere after nearly 22 years of cosmic exploration. Originally planned as a two-year mission, the space telescope transformed scientific understanding of black holes and cosmic explosions.
stories.title: NASA’s Swift telescope falls to Earth after nearly 22 years in space

stories.summary: A 12-week study found that consuming three daily servings of full-fat dairy did not adversely affect weight or cholesterol levels. Participants also experienced improvements in blood pressure and nutrient intake.
stories.title: For decades, we were told to avoid full-fat dairy. New research says otherwise

stories.summary: Computer simulations suggest that magnetic fields allow white dwarf stars to grow more massive than previously thought possible. The discovery helps explain the origin of unusually bright supernova explosions.
stories.title: Dead stars could break one of physics' most famous limits

stories.summary: Physicists have detected evidence of an extremely rare particle decay process after a 42-year search. The achievement opens new possibilities for studying subatomic physics at unprecedented scales.
stories.title: After 42 Years of Searching, Physicists Find Evidence of a One-in-10-Billion Particle Decay

stories.summary: A study indicates that low-dose rapamycin can improve brain blood flow in adults genetically predisposed to Alzheimer's disease. The four-week treatment demonstrated particularly strong benefits for female participants.
stories.title: An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin

stories.summary: Health Canada has approved Moderna's mRNA influenza vaccine and a combined flu and COVID-19 shot. Both vaccines are authorized for use in adults aged 50 and older.
stories.title: Health Canada approves Moderna's mRNA flu and flu-COVID combo vaccines

stories.summary: Researchers at a McMaster University lab are developing new methods to make life-saving therapeutics more affordable. The team has been collaborating with industry partners to transform medicine manufacturing.
stories.title: Inside the McMaster lab that is making life-saving medicine more affordable

stories.summary: Archaeologists have discovered vast Ice Age cave art hiding in plain sight. The find provides new insights into population sizes and regional artistic expression during the Paleolithic period.
stories.title: Archaeologists Discover Vast Ice Age Cave Art Hiding in Plain Sight

stories.summary: A McMaster University researcher is leading a national project backed by $24 million to transform Indigenous sexual health care. The initiative aims to lower rates of infections by centering Indigenous communities in health research.
stories.title: McMaster researcher receives $24M to transform Indigenous sexual health research and care

stories.summary: A guest retreat in Montana provides meaningful employment for autistic individuals as wranglers, concierges, and guides. The program empowers staff while offering guests an immersive wilderness experience.
stories.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides

stories.summary: Sandwich tern populations on England's south coast have recovered from zero to over 700 birds following severe avian flu losses. Dedicated conservation efforts have enabled these and other seabird species to successfully repopulate the site.
stories.title: Seabird Sees Miracle Recovery After Avian Flu Wiped Them Out

stories.summary: Scientists have developed a revolutionary gel that can regrow lost tooth enamel using minerals naturally found in saliva. The treatment could potentially repair damaged teeth, prevent decay, and reduce sensitivity.
stories.title: Goodbye, cavities? Scientists create gel that could regrow tooth enamel

stories.summary: Scientists have solved a decades-old mystery by discovering a hidden immune system defense that protects healthy cells from excessive inflammation. The discovery could lead to new medical treatments for inflammatory conditions and cancer.
stories.title: Scientists solve 30-year-old mystery and discover a hidden defense against inflammation

stories.summary: An international research team established clinical guidelines for using bacteria-killing viruses to treat antibiotic-resistant infections. Early applications of this phage therapy show encouraging results against dangerous superbugs.
stories.title: Scientists turn viruses into weapons against deadly superbugs

stories.summary: Researchers successfully generated net-positive electricity using heat from an underwater volcano off the United States coast. The achievement marks a milestone in developing offshore volcanic geothermal power.
stories.title: World First: Underwater Volcano Off US Coast Generates Net-Positive Electricity

stories.summary: A long-time volunteer is reflecting on nearly five decades of participating in Toronto's Santa Claus Parade. Preparations are currently underway for the 122nd edition of the annual spectacle.
stories.title: Toronto Santa Claus Parade volunteer recalls nearly 50 years walking in the annual spectacle

stories.summary: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk completed a spacewalk lasting over six hours outside the International Space Station. The operation marked his second successful spacewalk within two weeks.
stories.title: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk completes second spacewalk, more than six hours long

stories.summary: Sweden is returning a trove of Benin bronzes and Indigenous remains to their countries of origin. Seventy-seven objects belonging to the Kallawaya people are being sent back to an archaeological museum in Bolivia.
stories.title: Sweden Returns Benin Bronze Trove to Nigeria, Indigenous Remains to Bolivia

stories.summary: New Amazon mapping data shows that cacao cultivation is expanding without causing deforestation in Brazil. Farmers are successfully reviving degraded pastures instead of clearing rainforests for chocolate production.
stories.title: Amazon mapping shows cacao expansion without deforestation in Brazil

stories.summary: A Brock University researcher is investigating how protein breakdown in blood vessels contributes to heart disease and stroke. The study compares vessel protein changes to rust inside water pipes.
stories.title: Canada Research Chair investigating how ‘protein rust’ may lead to heart disease and stroke

stories.summary: A social enterprise leader in Mali has won United Nations recognition for her work in restoring degraded land. She uses agroforestry techniques to combat drier soils and create jobs for women and youth.
stories.title: Mali’s ‘Moringa Queen’ wins UN recognition for restoring degraded land

stories.summary: Researchers are studying butterfly wings to design paint coatings that do not rely on chemical pigments. This bio-inspired approach could lead to safer and more sustainable manufacturing methods.
stories.title: The butterfly effect: a brighter way to make paint?

stories.summary: Scientists used a hospital CT scanner to solve the secret behind a 400-year-old padlock recovered from a Welsh shipwreck. The non-invasive scan allowed researchers to inspect the internal mechanism without causing damage.
stories.title: 400-yo Shipwreck Puzzle Finally Cracked After More Than 20 Years of Mystery

stories.summary: NASA astronauts aboard the International Space Station will answer STEM questions submitted by Florida students during a live stream. The educational event aims to inspire youth through direct interaction with space researchers.
stories.title: NASA Astronauts to Answer Questions from Florida Students

stories.summary: Pixies bass player Emma Richardson is launching a new art exhibition featuring her large-scale paintings. The musician's canvases explore themes of terror and awe as part of her multi-vocational career.
stories.title: Is that an explosion, an implosion or an orgasm? Pixies bass-player Emma Richardson’s realm-leaping life in painting

stories.summary: A United States city has successfully transformed a former desert highway into a leafy, walkable oasis. The nine-block boulevard now hosts 250 enterprises, including restaurants, museums, and performing arts centers.
stories.title: ‘It’s kind of a melting pot’: how one US city transformed a highway into a leafy oasis

stories.summary: Scientists developed a microscopic filtration membrane that separates crude oil at room temperature. The process could cut refining energy consumption by nearly 32 percent and significantly lower carbon emissions.
stories.title: Scientists discover that a clogged filter could revolutionize oil refining
